blocs: You can ask an AI (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini…) for help when you are stuck in Yop2D. But an AI does not know Yop2D well: on its own, it sometimes invents nodes that do not exist. This guide shows you how to give it what it needs to answer **correctly**.
An AI can be wrong, even when well prepared. **Always test** what it tells you. And never paste personal information: what you write is sent to the AI service you use.
Step 1: give it the right file
Yop2D has a file written **for AIs**: it explains how the engine works, the most common mistakes, and lists **every node** with its exact name. Its address is:
**If your AI can open links**, start your message with: "Read https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/llms-full.txt first".
**If it cannot** (many cannot): open the link in your browser, select all the text, copy it and paste it at the start of the conversation. The file is long: that is normal.
The more precise your message, the better the answer. Here is a template to adapt:

"Read https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/llms-full.txt first. I am making a game with Yop2D (version 1.0.xxxx, I am a beginner, on a phone). **What I want to do:** … **What happens:** … **What I already tried:** … Answer in simple steps, with the exact names of Yop2D buttons and nodes, no code. If you are not sure a node exists, say so."
**Your version:** it is written on the start screen. Some nodes are only in the test version.
**One problem per message:** an AI answers small questions better.
**Say what you wanted, and what happens instead:** it helps the most.
Describing nodes with words is hard. There is an easier way:
Open the **Blueprint** of the scene concerned.
Tap the **{ }** button (top right): it shows your nodes as text.
Copy this text and paste it into your conversation with the AI, with your question.
If needed, add a **screenshot** of the node's settings window (AIs that can read images use it well).
Follow the steps **one by one** and test after each step.

If the AI mentions a node or setting you cannot find: ask for its **exact name**, then look for it in the [node list](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/noeuds/en.html). It may be wrong, or the node may only exist in the test version.
Tap **☰ → Check my game**: Yop2D lists what is missing (variable, object, file, node connected to nothing).
Still stuck? Tell the AI what you did and what happened, and it can correct itself.

If it still does not work, ask on the **Yop2D Discord**: give your version, what you wanted to do and, if possible, your exported project (start screen → your project → Export). Your question also helps improve the guides and the file for AIs.
The [beginner guides](guide:plateforme) show how to make real little games, step by step.
